protocol_type: Controller-mastered command-driven low-power mobile memory bus. Commands are encoded on a 7-bit double-data-rate CA bus (CA[6:0]) referenced to a quarter-speed differential CK; each command occupies two CA transfers (rising then falling CK edge). Data transfers are double-data-rate on DQ, framed by a separately-enabled full-speed WCK on writes and a DRAM-driven RDQS on reads. There is no CKE pin; low-power entry is a CA command bounded by CS.

command_encoding.transfer: Double data rate referenced to quarter-speed CK: each command uses one rising-edge and one falling-edge CA transfer.

field_legend.WRX: Write X (fill burst all-zero / all-one, no data transfer)
field_legend.WXSA / WXSB: Write X select (value to be written for the X-fill)

commands.name: Power-down entry
commands.notes: CA-bus power-down (PD); no CKE; lasts until CS next goes high.

commands.name: Read DQ Calibration
commands.notes: Returns a fixed DQ calibration pattern.

commands.name: Multi-purpose command
commands.notes: Carries OP[7:0]; used for ZQ calibration etc.

commands.name: Self-refresh entry
commands.notes: Enter self-refresh; PD/DSE select power-down vs deep-sleep.

commands.name: Refresh
commands.notes: REFab (AB) or REFpb (per-bank round-robin); RFM selects Refresh Management.

commands.name: Column Address Select
commands.notes: Carries WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR, WRX, WXSA/WXSB; prepares WCK sync — does NOT select a column.

commands.name: Read-32
commands.notes: Double-length (BL32) read; start position via C0/B3.

wck_synchronization.WS_FS: Free-Start — start WCK immediately; may precede multiple reads/writes (multiple banks).
wck_synchronization.WS_RD: Read-optimized — optimize WCK timing for an immediately following read.
wck_synchronization.WS_WR: Write-optimized — optimize WCK timing for an immediately following write.
wck_synchronization.rule: The CAS command carries WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR to lock internal WCK to CK before the high-speed transfer. Unlike LPDDR4, the CAS command in LPDDR5 comes BEFORE the read/write and primarily serves this synchronization role (it does not select a column).

channels.name: CK_t, CK_c
channels.description: Quarter-speed differential master clock; CA sampled at double data rate relative to CK.

channels.name: WCK_t, WCK_c
channels.description: Full-speed differential Write Clock (4x CK); enabled only when a transfer is imminent; frames write data and pre-synchronizes reads.

channels.name: RDQS_t, RDQS_c
channels.description: Full-speed differential Read Strobe; DRAM-driven, edge-aligned with read data; enabled only during reads.

channels.name: CS
channels.description: Chip select (active high); marks the first command cycle; bounds low-power-mode duration (replaces CKE).

channels.name: CA[6:0]
channels.description: 7-bit double-data-rate command/address bus; a command occupies two CA transfers.

channels.name: DQ[15:0]
channels.description: Data bus per channel, two x8 byte groups; double data rate at the WCK/RDQS rate.

channels.name: DMI
channels.description: Data Mask / Data Bus Inversion per byte group; write mask + DBI.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no per-beat handshake; commands are committed on the CA bus referenced to CK; data follows at deterministic latency relative to WCK/RDQS.
Before a high-speed transfer the controller issues a WCK2CK synchronization (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR via CAS); the DRAM locks its internal WCK phase during this window.
READ data appears at the programmed read latency, framed by the DRAM-driven RDQS edge-aligned with DQ.
WRITE data is launched at the programmed write latency, framed by the controller-driven WCK.
tCCD_L/tRRD_L (same bank group) and tCCD_S/tRRD_S (different bank group) govern command spacing in bank-group mode.

frame_format.command_frame: Two CA transfers (rising + falling CK) on the 7-bit CA bus encode one command; CS high marks the first cycle.
frame_format.data_frame_BL16: 16-beat burst on DQ framed by WCK (write) or RDQS (read) at full speed (both edges).
frame_format.data_frame_BL32: 32-beat double-length burst; reads may start within the 32-word-aligned burst via C0/B3.
frame_format.row_open_requires_two_ACT: Opening a row requires Activate-1 then Activate-2.

comparison_to_lpddr4: LPDDR4 column names C0-C9 are renamed in LPDDR5 to B0-B3 and C0-C5; writes start at a multiple-of-16 address (B0-B3 zero); reads may use a non-zero B3.
LPDDR5 widens the CA bus to 7 bits at double data rate, so commands arrive at the same cadence as LPDDR4 despite the quarter-speed CK.
In LPDDR5 the CAS command precedes the read/write and synchronizes WCK (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR); in LPDDR4 the CAS-2 command followed the column command.
LPDDR5 provides one set of full-speed WCK clocks per byte (vs per 16 bits in LPDDR4).
